review_status: draft v1 - fast aggressive coastal schooling predator

profile.diet: Mullet, menhaden, pilchards, squids, and crabs
profile.behavior: Aggressive, fast-swimming schooling predator that blitzes bait in inlets, bays, surf lines, and coastal beaches.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, in warm tropical range favored by jack crevalle.
factors.value_notes: The Florida Museum species account reports adult occurrence at approximately 18–33.6 °C and larval occurrence at 20.4–29.4 °C. This provides species-specific thermal context, but occurrence is not a preferred-temperature or catch-response curve and the configured 20–32 °C range / 24–30 °C ideal are not directly validated.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, in shallow coastal and inlet waters.
factors.value_notes: The Florida Museum account reports occurrence along the continental shelf and depths to about 100 m, with habitat varying by life stage; SCDNR describes both offshore and estuarine use. This supports broad coastal depth context but does not validate the configured 0.5–30 m range or 1–15 m ideal as a universal preference.

value_text.peak: It is peak jack crevalle run season.

factors.value_notes: FWC reports peak offshore spawning from March through September in subtropical waters; SCDNR describes seasonal north/south movement and summer occurrence in South Carolina. These sources support seasonal reproductive and migration context, not the configured March–November presence window or April–May/September–October peak catch scores in South Florida. Retain the monthly map as a provisional seasonal screening proxy.

text.day: It is full daylight, when fish feed actively.
text.dawn: It is dawn, a low-light time when fish feed actively.
text.dusk: It is dusk, a low-light time when fish feed actively.

text.rising: The tide is rising, bringing in fresh water and bait.
text.falling: The tide is falling, flushing bait out through structure.

timing.note: Patterns reported by local captains and fishing writers, not tested by studies.
